title: DESL 0.2 — Designer Specification Language
description: Specifications ($defs/Specification): one designer type each, written by a tool engineer. DESL defines every construct it uses; storage is FBL's, through $defs/Persistence. See DESL-specification.md.

Specification.description: The root of a DESL document: one designer type, with the DESL version, the type's identity, its metamodel, how its documents are stored, its constraints, its surface, its operations and its functions. See section 3.1.

desl.description: The DESL version the specification is written in: 0.1, or 0.2, which adds the hierarchy surface, counted ids, mentions, move and persistence.settings. See section 2.7.

operations.description: The designer's operations, by id. See section 8.1.

functions.description: Reusable CEL functions, by name. See section 3.3.

Language.description: The identity of the designer type: a globally unique id, a SemVer version, the origin <vendor>/<type> that every registration of its documents and every DED definition names, and its label, documentation, locales, authors, licence, homepage, icon and limits. See section 3.2.

origin.description: The designer type's origin, <vendor>/<type>, such as etalii/knowledge. See section 3.2.

icon.description: The designer type's icon, by name. See section 3.2.

limits.description: Limits a host applies. See section 2.5.

Function.description: A reusable CEL function, called by its name: its positional parameters, its result type and its body, which sees only its parameters and, when listed in uses, document. A function may call functions declared before it, never itself. See section 3.3.

Metamodel.description: What a document of the designer type can hold: the attributes of the document itself, enumerations, and element types by name. Nothing in it is drawn connected: a link between elements is a reference attribute. See section 4.1.

document.description: The attributes of the document as a whole, and (DESL 0.2) the types its own elements may be. See section 4.1.

children.description: (DESL 0.2) The types the document's own elements may be, checked by std.containment. See section 4.6.

ElementType.description: A kind of element a document holds: its label, icon, attributes, the element types it contains, and the attribute that names one of its elements. See section 4.5.

Containment.description: Which element types an element contains, whether their order is kept, and the named slots its children are kept in. A contained element has one parent and is deleted with it. See section 4.6.

additionalProperties.description: A named slot: the element types it holds.

Attribute.description: One named value of an element, of the document or of an operation's parameters: a primitive type, an enumeration or an element type (a reference, section 4.7), with a default, whether it is required or a list, and its facets. See section 4.3.

type.description: A primitive type of section 4.2, an enumeration or an element type. See section 4.3.

timezone.description: How a datetime value's zone is kept: utc, or preserve, which keeps the offset it was written with. See section 4.2.

Mentions.description: (DESL 0.2) A string or text attribute whose value names elements by id: the matches of pattern in which its group id takes part, naming elements of types. See section 4.3.

Enum.description: An enumeration: its values in display order, by key. See section 4.4.

EnumValue.description: One value of an enumeration: its stored form when that differs from its key, its label and its icon. See section 4.4.

Persistence.description: How the designer's documents are stored: through FBL, one binding per format family, with the type map, the ids and (DESL 0.2) what the registration keeps. See section 5.

typeMap.description: The bindings' types mapped onto the metamodel, by the binding's type name. See section 5.2.

settings.description: (DESL 0.2) The part of the model a document's registration keeps, by the name of the registration block each part is kept in. See section 5.5.

Setting.description: (DESL 0.2) What one registration block keeps: a list, whose entries are the elements of a type, or a state, one attribute of the elements of some types keyed by their ids. See section 5.5.

oneOf.description: A list: the elements of type are the block's entries, key and value naming the attributes of an entry's key and value; initial, the elements a document has while the block is absent, by their attribute values.
A state: the attribute of the elements of the types of, keyed by their ids; only a value that differs from the default is kept.

TypeMapEntry.description: How one type of the bindings maps onto the metamodel: what its entries become (the document, a header, an unreadable entry or an element type), its attributes by their model names, and the attributes the binding keeps that are not the model's. See section 5.2.

IdStrategy.description: How elements get their ids: the strategy for every type, the text form of generated ids, whether they are kept once made, what happens to an element read without one, and per-type rules. See section 5.3.

IdRule.description: The id rule of one element type: its strategy, the expression of a derived id, (DESL 0.2) the prefix, digits, mark and placeholder of a counted id, whether the id is ephemeral, and the refusal shown when a gesture would store one. See sections 5.3.2 and 5.3.5.

prefix.description: (DESL 0.2) counter: what every id of the type starts with.

digits.description: (DESL 0.2) counter: the least number of digits of a new number. Default 1.

mark.description: (DESL 0.2) counter: the string attribute of the document that holds the last id given.

placeholder.description: (DESL 0.2) counter: what a writer puts after the prefix in place of a number.

Constraints.description: The designer's validity rules, in order, with their default severity and whether a document with errors may be saved. See section 6.1.

defaults.description: Defaults for every rule: its severity and when it is evaluated.

Constraint.description: One validity rule in CEL: what it is evaluated for, when, the condition that must hold, and the severity, code and message of each finding it reports. See section 6.2.

Operation.description: A named command that one gesture of the surface runs: what it applies to, its parameters, why it may be unavailable, the confirmation it asks for and its actions, run as one transaction. See section 8.1.

Confirmation.description: The question asked before an operation runs, and when: only while when holds and, with count, when count is at least threshold. See section 8.3.

Action.description: One step of an operation, from a closed set: set, unset, create, delete, reorder, (DESL 0.2) move, let, if and forEach. Every value is an Expression, and every action may carry when. See section 8.2.

reorder.description: The element's new place among its siblings.

move.description: (DESL 0.2) The element's new parent, slot and place: after or before a sibling there, else last. See section 8.2.

Surface.description: How the model is laid out for the user: one shape per kind, a table (sections 7.2 to 7.6) or (DESL 0.2) a hierarchy (section 7.7). See section 7.

Table.description: The table kind of surface: rows and columns, with a cell at each crossing, and views that store how it is shown. See sections 7.2 to 7.6.

Hierarchy.description: (DESL 0.2) The hierarchy kind of surface: levels drawn as boxes that contain boxes, entries, labels, notes, what is collapsed, stored filters, the widths of the columns of levels and whether ids are shown. See section 7.7.

HierarchyMembers.description: (DESL 0.2) The levels or the entries of a hierarchy: their element type, and its title and description attributes. See section 7.7.

Labels.description: (DESL 0.2) A label attribute of a hierarchy: the types it is on, the element type of its list's members with their name and colour attributes, and the prefix of a filter's word for a member. See sections 7.7.2 and 7.7.3.

Notes.description: (DESL 0.2) The notes of a hierarchy: their element type, and the attributes of what a note is about, its kind, text, detail and whether it is resolved. See section 7.7.

Filters.description: (DESL 0.2) The stored filters of a hierarchy: their element type, and the attributes of a filter's name and query. See section 7.7.3.

Widths.description: (DESL 0.2) The widths of a hierarchy's columns of levels: their element type, and the attributes of a column's depth and its width in pixels. See section 7.7.1.

Columns.description: The columns of a table: their element type and the attributes that name them, type them, mark the title column and the parent column, and the options a choice may take. See section 7.3.

options.description: The element type of a column's options, and the attributes that name and colour one.

Cells.description: The cells of a table: their element type, the reference attribute naming the column, and the element type of one of several values. See section 7.3.

Views.description: The views of a table: their element type, the attribute naming one, the document attribute naming the active one, and the element types of their settings by role. See section 7.4.

ValueType.description: What a column's cells hold: the key of the value, whether there are several, the editor, the filter comparisons, the sort order and the conversions to other value types. See section 7.5.

Conversion.description: What a value becomes when its column's value type changes. See section 7.6.

SimpleId.description: A name that is a valid CEL identifier: types, attributes, parameters, operations, functions. See section 2.2.

QualifiedId.description: Dot-separated names, hyphens allowed after the first character: language ids and finding codes. See section 2.2.

TypeRef.description: The name of an element type of the metamodel. See section 2.2.

TypeRefs.description: One element type or a list of them. See section 2.2.

LocalizedText.description: A human-facing text: a string, or a map from BCP 47 language tag to string. See section 2.3.

Message.description: A sentence or label shown to the user: a LocalizedText, or CEL returning one. See section 2.3.

Reason.description: Why something is refused or unavailable: a Message that always applies, or one that applies while when holds. See section 2.3.

anyOf.description: A reason that applies while when holds.

Doc.description: Documentation of any object: a LocalizedText (its summary) or an object with a summary, a description, a rationale, examples, links and tags. See section 2.4.

Expression.description: CEL: a string of CEL source, or an object with it, an expected result type and documentation. See section 2.5.

CelValue.description: CEL source with an expected result type and documentation. See section 2.5.
